chapter_title: Concerning these Names: God, Rich One, and Angel;

3.original: [in the land of light, and there is no measure to]
3.content: in the land of light, and there is no measure to

spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Three Degrees of Divine Proceeding

**¶3:** There are three infinite degrees of reception [GAP-1: REVIEW — within the heaven of Divine Wisdom, and they are without limit in] their extent.

**¶4:** Those which are called "celestial goods" are the primary qualities of good that Divine Love has caused to proceed from Himself. He has formed them according to the very pattern of His own infinite perfection.

**¶5:** Those which are named "abundant [GAP-2: spiritual goods]" are the derivative states that proceed from the first celestial goods of Divine Love; for when Divine Love had caused the primary goods to proceed, those goods themselves brought forth further states of reception. These derivative states are called "abundances of good."

**¶6:** These abundances of good have in turn brought forth their own derivative states, which are called "ministering truths." These are the three infinite degrees of reception that exist within the heaven of Divine Wisdom. There is no finite measure that can compass them.

**¶7:** Hear further: those who in another sense are called "celestial goods" are the divine powers that have proceeded forth from Divine Love — the emanations which He caused to go out into the contest against evil and falsity, and which overcame the enmity of hell.

**¶8:** The "abundances of good" in this sense are the derivative states proceeding from these first living Divine Truths. These abundances also descended and accomplished and fulfilled the purpose of the Divine, in both the interior states and the exterior states.

**¶9:** The "ministering truths" are the derivative states proceeding from the abundances of good, which themselves had come forth from the three living Divine Truths.

**¶10:** Again, "celestial goods" names all the goods that belong to the province of Divine Love Proceeding.

**¶11:** "Ministering truths" names all the truths that belong to the province of Divine Wisdom Proceeding.

**¶12:** "Abundances of good" names all the fullnesses of spiritual wealth that belong to the province of Divine Use Proceeding.

---

**Translator's note:** The entire chapter describes the threefold proceeding of the Divine through three discrete degrees — what Swedenborg calls celestial, spiritual, and natural, or love, wisdom, and use. Paragraphs 3–6 describe these three degrees *as they exist at rest within the Divine order itself*. Paragraphs 7–9 describe the same three degrees *as they go forth into activity against the hells*. Paragraphs 10–12 assign each degree to its governing Divine attribute: the Great Spirit corresponds to Divine Love (the celestial), the Beloved of the Lights to Divine Wisdom (the spiritual), and the glorious Ambassador to Divine Use as it mediates between interior and exterior states (the natural). The triadic structure maps precisely onto the three heavens and onto the will, understanding, and act in the regenerating person.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: There are these three archetypes [in the land of light, and there is no measure to] them!
So, the ones who are called 'god', are the gods whom the Father has summoned from himself. He has established them after the likeness of his greatness.

Conversely, these who are named 'rich [ones]', are the evocations of the first rich gods of the Father; because, when the Father had summoned (the first), they themselves summoned evocations. They called them 'rich'.
They too, the rich ones, have summoned their evocations. They call them 'angel'. These are the three archetypes who occur in the land of light. There is no measure to apply to them!

Once again, listen! Other persons who are named 'god' are the emanations who have come from the Father; the evocations of the Father whom he summoned forth. They came out to the contest and humiliated the Enmity.

Conversely, the 'rich ones' are the evocations of these first living words. They too, the rich ones, have come and performed and fulfilled the pleasure of the greatness, in the worlds that are above and below.
On the other hand, the ones who are named the 'angels' are the evocations of the rich ones, who had come from the three living words.
Again, they are called 'god', all the gods who belong to the household of the Great Spirit.
Conversely, the ones who are called 'angel', are all the angels who belong to the household of the Beloved of the Lights.
The ones who are called 'rich', are all the rich ones who belong to the household of the glorious Ambassador.

fills.explanation: The parallel statement in ¶6 reads "These are the three archetypes who occur in the land of light. There is no measure to apply to them!" — confirming the editor's reconstruction almost verbatim.
The standard Kephalaia designation throughout the chapter (¶6, ¶8, ¶12) is "rich ones," and the spiritual reading's "abundant spiritual goods" maps to this term in the text's natural-plane register.
